ratio-order.title: ratio order
ratio-order.explanation: Each number in a ratio belongs to the name in the same position.
ratio-order.guidance: Write the names above the parts before calculating.
examples: Red : blue = 2 : 3 means 2 red parts for every 3 blue parts.

matching-parts.title: matching parts
matching-parts.explanation: The known amount may represent all the parts, one named share, or the difference between shares.
matching-parts.guidance: Match the amount before dividing: add parts for a total, select parts for one share, subtract parts for a difference.
examples: For 2 : 3, a total of £30 is 5 parts; a difference of £6 is 1 part.

one-part.title: one part
one-part.explanation: Ratio parts are equal-sized units. Knowing the value of one part lets you find any share.
one-part.guidance: Divide a known amount by its matching number of parts. Then multiply by the requested parts.
examples: Share £30 in the ratio 2 : 3. One part = £30 ÷ 5 = £6; the shares are £12 and £18.
